full_judgment: 6. Mr. BK Das, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submitted that Court of appeal below acted illegally in reversing the finding of the trial Court regarding defect of parties relying upon a Single Bench decision reported in 37 DLR 154. He further submitted that court of appeal below was not justified in granting Taka 45,000.00 as improvement costs to the petitioners. In this case there is no dispute that the pre-emptor-opposite parties are co-sharers in the case land and they impleaded the vendor and purchasers of the case land in the pre-emption case. From the khatian Ext. Ga (1) it transpires that Ambar Mia and others are the recorded owners whereas from kabala dated 22.10.81 Ext. 2 (Ka) it appears that common vendors purchased 15 decimals of land of the case plot from one of the recorded tenants. Mahmuda Khatun, wife of Israil Miah. Admittedly those recorded owners and their heirs and successors have not been impleaded in the pre-emption case. But the question is whether they are necessary parties in the case. Sub-section (2) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides for impleading all the co-sharer tenants or all the co-sharer-tenants as well as all the contiguous owners as parties in the pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Under sub-section (4) of the said section 96 remaining co-sharer tenants and the contiguous land owners have been given option of rateable pre-emption. Similarly, under sub-section (4) of section 24 of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act remaining co-sharer tenants have been given option to pray for rateable pre-emption. But there is no provision in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act similar to sub-section (2) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act Mr. Das strenuously argued that in the case of Hosna Ara Begum and others vs. Musammat Anowara Begum and others reported in 37 DLR 154 the question regarding option of the remaining co-sharers to pray for rateable pre-emption was not noticed and, as such, the said decision is required to be reconsidered. He submits that unless the remaining co-sharer tenants are made parties in a pre-emption case under section 24 of the said Act they would be deprived of the right to pray for rateable pre-emption. This argument though plausible is devoid of any merit. As there is no provision in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act to implead other co-sharers as party in a pre-emption proceeding it cannot be said that such a case will be bad for defect of party for not impleading the remaining co-sharer tenants. Any co-sharer tenant may apply for pre-emption under section 24 of the said Act by impleading the vendor as well as the purchaser of the disputed sale. In that case remaining co-sharer tenant or tenants may file separate case for pre-emption or pray for rateable pre-emption by being impleaded in the pre-emption case already filed by one of the co-sharers. I, therefore, find nothing to disagree with the said decision which is based on an unreported decision of the Appellate Division.
